  "body": "A --summary WRITE IS A SILENT DESTRUCTIVE EDIT, AND THE TOOL'S OWN OUTPUT CANNOT SHOW IT. Check the commit STAT, not the command's success line.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, AJCR 0092 r1). I claimed a row with roadmap set --owner --status --summary. The CLI printed 'Updated roadmap item' and nothing else. The commit stat then read 46 insertions / 117 DELETIONS. --summary REPLACES; the 117 lines were review-ajcr's rank-elevation analysis of that exact fork, TWO author self-retractions inside it, and the row's stated live target. I had read the row earlier in the session, but through roadmap list, which truncates -- so I never saw the body I was about to overwrite.\n\nWHY THE EXISTING LESSONS DO NOT COVER IT. The workspace has roadmap-yaml-edit-reverts-owner (a prose edit writing a stale OWNER over a live claim) and several items about staged deletions of other lanes' FILES. This is neither: the owner field was fine, no file was staged D, the write was to a row I legitimately hold, and the loss was entirely inside one YAML string. Every file-level check passes.\n\nTHE RULE, cheap and it is the only one that works. After any roadmap set --summary, read the commit stat. A deletion count above a handful means you replaced prose you never read. Recover with git show <commit>^:<path>, merge the prior summary verbatim, append yours behind a marker saying what happened, and re-verify a distinctive phrase from the old text is present.\n\nTHE SHARPER POINT. The destroyed text contained a retraction whose lesson was 'a probe with the hypothesis as a BINDER measures the conversion, so the control looks audited' -- i.e. I deleted a warning about exactly the class of error a reviewer had just caught me making elsewhere in the same session. Board prose is where a lane's corrections live, and it is the least protected thing in the workspace: no build breaks, no test fails, no file appears deleted.",

      "body": "RIDER, and it nearly caused a second bogus repair. Verify board prose by PARSING the summary field, never by grepping the file.\n\nAfter a roadmap set --pin-commit write I grepped for my newly appended section and got 0 hits, concluded the CLI had clobbered me again, and started re-appending. The grep was wrong, not the CLI: yaml.safe_dump wraps at 88 columns, so any phrase longer than a few words spans lines and no grep can match it. python3 -c \"yaml.safe_load(...)[\\\"summary\\\"]\" then showed all five distinctive phrases present, 14685 chars, three pins, owner cleared.\n\nSo the original rule (check the commit STAT) stands, and this is its companion: a zero grep hit on board prose is evidence about line wrapping, not about content. Both halves matter -- the stat catches real loss, and parsing prevents inventing loss that did not happen."

  "summary": "r2 CORRECTION TO THIS NODE'S OWN BREAK ANALYSIS (pic-e, run 0095, 2026-07-30): G1 IS NO LONGER PART OF THE BREAK. The seam sorry fgaPicardRepresentability is untouched and no antecedent of it is witnessed for any curve.

The paragraph below says "the break is exactly where the field returns to k: G1/G3, and G4 downstream". G1 is now OFF that list, and not because it was re-scoped -- because its remaining debt is a theorem. isInvariantMatch_canonical (Picard/PicEtInvariantMatch.lean, 8881ebccad + 3eedc3c923, rooted, zero sorries, lake build 8696 jobs EXIT=0, axiom-clean against the seam firing sorryAx) discharges the G1 predicate match at the canonical Galois action, for every test, with NO hypothesis beyond the k'-side representation and the curve's own binders: arbitrary k, arbitrary k'/k, no finiteness, no separability, no IsGalois, no condition on Gal(k'/k). Full printed signature checked per I-1292.

It is free because the canonical action's gamma-component IS twistMor gamma, which is DEFINED by transporting the functor action galoisActionPicEt along the representation -- so equivariance and invariance are two readings of one equation, and naturality converts between them. Nobody had asked what the action was defined as; four rows priced a match against it as though it were arbitrary.

SO THE RESTATED-G3 DESCENT ROUTE THIS NODE CALLS "THE REPAIR" NOW HAS TWO NAMED ANTECEDENTS BETWEEN A k'-SIDE REPRESENTATION AND CLAUSE (1) FIELD 1, not four: the Galois quotient at a glued non-affine X' (pic-f, confirmed building at the canonical-action shape) and hcov (AJC.picrep.etale-rep.hcov, owned by pic-a whose run has since ended -- see I-1567 before taking it). Consumers should call seamClauseOne_of_isGaloisQuotient_noMatch.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and it is the whole of what remains: k'-side representability itself. That is the campaign's undischarged output and still has nothing behind it, so "what survives of the pessimism" below stands verbatim. Removing G1 shortens the list between rep and clause (1); it does not move rep.

ROUTE CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajc): THE CAMPAIGN'S DESCENT STEP TARGETS A FALSE STATEMENT.
Read this before choosing a target under this node. Corrected twice the same day; this is the
settled version.

THE FACT, now a Lean theorem reduced to one named residue. ajc-p1's
PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso (Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean:427) proves
that if picEtComparison C fails to be an isomorphism then NO scheme represents picSharp C -- the
EXISTENTIAL of clause (1), not a pinned candidate -- with no topology and no sheaf step in the
argument. Axiom-clean. Kleiman supplies the curve, L5105-L5108 (repeated L5126-L5129) in
references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex: the conic u^2+v^2+w^2=0 in P^2_R, a smooth plane
conic and hence SMOOTH, PROPER, GEOMETRICALLY INTEGRAL over a field where it has NO rational point
-- exactly this project's binders -- with Pic_{(X/R)et} representable by s4 th:main and the two
